Rozine Terms and Conditions

Version terms-2026-11-23-r2 · Effective 23 November 2026 · Issued by Rozine Technologies Ltd (TIN 156642791), Kigali, Rwanda

These Terms are the agreement between you and Rozine Technologies Ltd ("Rozine", "we", "us"). They apply to everyone who uses Rozine: investors, businesses, Audit Partners and anyone who opens an account. Please read them with our Privacy Notice and our Disclaimers. When you sign up, you tick a box to agree to each of the three. We record the version you agreed to and the exact time.

The short version

  • Rozine is a marketplace. It connects Rwandan businesses that need short-term finance with people who want to lend to them. Rozine never lends its own money.
  • When you invest, you lend to a business through a note. The business repays you, not Rozine.
  • Investing is risky. You can lose all the money you invest. Nothing on Rozine is guaranteed.
  • Rozine gives no investment advice. Every rating, return and limit comes from a published formula and facts checked by an independent accountant.
  • Rozine earns only the fees listed in section 8. They are always shown in Rwandan francs before you confirm anything.

1. About Rozine

1.1. Who we are. Rozine Technologies Ltd is a private limited company registered in Rwanda (TIN 156642791).

1.2. The CMA sandbox. Rozine runs in the Capital Market Authority's Fintech Regulatory Sandbox, which the CMA admitted it to, under the limits the CMA sets. Being in the sandbox is not a licence or an endorsement by the CMA.

1.3. What Rozine is not. Rozine is not a bank, a microfinance institution, a deposit-taker or an insurer. Your wallet and your notes are not insured by the Government of Rwanda, the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) or the CMA.

2. How Rozine follows the rules for crowdfunding platforms

Platforms like Rozine must follow clear rules that protect investors and businesses. Here is each rule and how Rozine meets it.

  1. Investor money. The rule: the platform must not hold investor funds. How Rozine does it: all customer money is to be held in a segregated client account at a licensed Rwandan commercial bank, kept apart from Rozine's own money. We are in talks with GT Bank to provide this account; no agreement has been signed yet. Rozine will not take real customer money until that account is open. Only Rozine's earned, disclosed fees ever move from the client account to Rozine.
  2. The platform's own interest. The rule: no raising funds for itself, and no holding interests in the businesses it lists. How Rozine does it: Rozine never raises money on its own platform, never lends its own money and never holds a stake or a note in any business on Rozine.
  3. No guarantees. The rule: no guaranteed returns and no guaranteed success of a raise. How Rozine does it: Rozine guarantees neither. A risk warning appears on every listing. If a raise does not reach 100% within 30 days, every investor gets all of their money back.
  4. No investment advice. The rule: the platform must not advise or recommend. How Rozine does it: Rozine gives no advice. Each business carries a rating label, such as Strong, Stable or Distressed, produced by a published formula from facts verified by a Certified Public Accountant (CPA). A label is a description, not a recommendation.
  5. Terms of the offer. The rule: the business sets the terms; the platform may set admission requirements. How Rozine does it: the business chooses how much to ask for, the term (3 to 6 months) and whether to accept the offer. The return comes from the verified risk and is never more than 15% for the whole term. A note is sized so the business's verified cash covers each instalment at least 1.5 times.
  6. Eligible businesses and checks. The rule: established small and medium businesses, with checks on the business and its directors. How Rozine does it: Rozine lists Rwandan businesses with verified annual revenue of RWF 30,000,000 or more. Their directors and owners are identified and screened. The rating looks at how long the business has traded, its profit, how steady that profit is, and its size. A Rwandan CPA visits and verifies each business in person before it is listed.
  7. Disclosure. The rule: a full offer document before the offer opens. How Rozine does it: every raise has a Rozine prospectus with CPA-verified financials. The business's official representative signs it, and it is then locked, dated and kept on record. Investors can read it before they invest.
  8. Withdrawal. The rule: a 48-hour cooling-off period. How Rozine does it: investors can withdraw a commitment at any time, for a full refund, until the raise reaches 100%. That is longer than 48 hours for most raises.
  9. Investor limits. The rule: limits set by the platform. How Rozine does it: no investor may hold more than 50% of any raise. We will add a limit for retail investors if the CMA requires one.
  10. Selling early. The rule: secondary trading is allowed under fair, published rules. How Rozine does it: sellers set their own price, never above what the note still has to pay out. The seller pays a 2% fee and the buyer pays nothing. The rules are in section 4.9.
  11. Use of funds and records. The rule: reasonable steps to check how funds are used, and full records. How Rozine does it: a CPA visits every business with a live note each month and seals a report for investors before each repayment. Every ledger entry is permanent: it can never be edited or deleted, and any correction is a new entry.
  12. Instruments. The rule: shares, debt and other approved instruments are allowed. How Rozine does it: Rozine focuses on short-term debt, because it is the instrument Rwandan small businesses and first-time investors understand and use most.

3. Your account

3.1. Who can open an account. You must be at least 18 years old. An organisation, such as a company investing as an institution, signs up through a person who can act for it.

3.2. One account, your own details. Your account is personal to you. Keep your password and two-factor sign-in safe. Tell us at once at info@rozine.rw if you think someone else has used your account.

3.3. Verification. Before you can fund a wallet, invest, raise or carry out audits, we verify who you are (KYC) or, for a business, the business itself (KYB). Individuals use a Rwandan National ID or a passport. We screen people and businesses against sanctions and politically exposed person lists before activation and from time to time after that.

3.4. Your own money accounts. Deposits come only from, and withdrawals go only to, bank or Mobile Money accounts held in your own name (or your business's name). A payment from someone else's account is held and reviewed.

3.5. Before verification. Until you are verified, you can look around but you cannot move money, invest, raise or trade.

3.6. Fair use. Do not give false information, use someone else's identity, try to get around a limit (for example by using several accounts), or interfere with the platform. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these Terms or fails a compliance check, and we report suspicious activity to the Financial Intelligence Centre as the law requires.

4. For investors

4.1. What you buy. A note is a fixed-return loan to one business. The business owes each holder directly, in proportion to the units they hold. One unit is RWF 5,000 of principal. Units are recorded on Rozine's ledger.

4.2. Risks you confirm. After your identity is verified, and before your wallet opens, you confirm on one screen that you understand these five statements: I can lose all the money I invest. There is no guarantee or collateral. Returns are paid only if the business pays. I may not find a buyer if I want to sell early. Rozine operates in the CMA sandbox under limits. If this wording changes, you see the new wording once and confirm it again.

4.3. Return and schedule. Each note pays a fixed total return, set when the note is issued, in equal monthly instalments over 3, 4, 5 or 6 months. The full schedule is shown before you commit.

4.4. Raises. A raise is open for up to 30 days or until it is 100% funded. If it is not fully funded after 30 days, every commitment goes back to the investors' wallets in full, and nobody pays a fee.

4.5. Committing. Every investment is a whole number of RWF 5,000 units. You can put several notes in a cart and pay for them in one checkout. Before you pay, you see the amount, every fee in RWF, your net return, the full schedule and the risk warning. If any figure changes before you confirm, the payment is blocked and the screen refreshes. Paying confirms you have read the prospectus for each note in the cart.

4.6. Withdrawing a commitment. The money you commit is set aside in your wallet. Until the raise reaches 100%, you can withdraw your commitment at any time and get all of it back. Once the raise reaches 100%, your commitment is final and the money goes to the business.

4.7. Payouts. On each due date, the instalment is collected from the business. Your share is paid into your wallet, less the earnings fee in section 8.

4.8. Late payment and default. If a business pays late, a late charge of 5% of the unpaid amount is added on the due date, on day 7 and on day 30, up to 15% of the instalment. Every franc of late charges collected goes to the note's holders. Rozine takes none of it. If the arrears are not cleared by day 31, the note is in default and legal recovery starts. Everything recovered goes to holders in proportion to their units. Late charges and recoveries are paid only when they are actually collected. Rozine does not cover shortfalls.

4.9. Selling early (resale). When resale is open, you may list units of a note that is not late, in default or disputed. You choose how many units to sell and the price per unit, in whole francs, up to what the note still has to pay out per unit. A listing lasts 7 days. A buyer's purchase reserves the units for 5 minutes and uses money already in their wallet. The money and the units change hands in one step. The seller pays 2% of the sale price. There is no fee for listing, cancelling or letting a listing expire. Trading in a note pauses around each due date until that month's payouts are posted. A sale needs a buyer, so it is never guaranteed.

4.10. Withdrawing from your wallet. Each withdrawal is between RWF 1,000 and RWF 2,000,000 and goes only to your own verified account. Rozine charges no withdrawal fee. Your provider's charge is shown before you confirm. An unusual request may be held for up to 24 hours for review. Money committed to an open raise or reserved for a purchase cannot be withdrawn.

5. For businesses

5.1. Who may apply. The business must be registered in Rwanda, have verified annual revenue of RWF 30,000,000 or more, and upload 36 months of bank and Mobile Money statements (12 months for a repeat issuer).

5.2. Official representative. One official representative acts for the business for every approval, acceptance and dispute. The person who signs up for the business confirms that they can bind it. A second signatory is never required on Rozine.

5.3. Your offer. Rozine's engine works out the rating, the amount and the return from a published formula and the verified figures. No staff member can change the result or override a failed check. The amount is the lowest of what you asked for, what your verified cash can carry at a coverage of 1.5 times each instalment, 35% of your verified annual revenue and RWF 100,000,000, in multiples of RWF 5,000. You choose the term (3 to 6 months) and whether to accept.

5.4. Prospectus. Before your raise opens, your official representative signs the prospectus. It is then locked and shown to investors.

5.5. Monthly checks. While a note is outstanding, you share the month's figures about 10 days before each due date, and a CPA verifies them in person. The CPA's sealed report is published to investors before the due date. You can dispute a sealed report within 24 hours; after that it is final. Rozine may also send a CPA for an unannounced visit, and you must give them access.

5.6. Disbursement. When your raise reaches 100%, the money is paid to your verified account, less the 3% platform fee.

5.7. Repayment. You repay the principal plus the fixed return in equal monthly instalments. Each instalment is collected from your Rozine wallet on its due date, and we remind you to fund the wallet beforehand. If your wallet is short, what is there is collected and the rest becomes overdue; money that arrives later is collected straight away. You may repay the whole balance early, but the return owed does not reduce.

5.8. Late payment and default. Late charges are added as described in section 4.8. They all go to your investors. If you clear all arrears and late charges before day 31, the note returns to normal. If not, the note is in default on day 31 and legal recovery starts under Rwandan law.

5.9. Repeat raises. A new raise can open only after your previous note is fully repaid. It can be at most 1.5 times the principal of that note.

6. For Audit Partners

6.1. Audit Partners are independent CPAs licensed by ICPAR. They sign Rozine's engagement terms separately, inside the Auditor app, before they take any visit. Those engagement terms add to these Terms.

6.2. An Audit Partner must stay independent of every business they verify and declare any conflict.

7. Information on Rozine

7.1. Business figures shown on Rozine come from statements the business uploaded and the CPA's checks. Rozine cannot promise that every figure is free of error.

7.2. Forecasts, schedules and returns are what is contractually due. They are not promises that the business will pay.

7.3. The full list of warnings that apply to Rozine is on our Disclaimers page.

8. Fees

Rozine earns only these fees. Each one is shown in RWF before you confirm.

Who pays Fee When
Business 3% of the principal raised Taken from the money paid out when the raise reaches 100%
Business No application fee While Rozine is in the sandbox
Investor Earnings fee on the return part of each payout, never on principal: 15% (under RWF 1M), 12% (RWF 1M to 5M), 10% (RWF 5M to 25M), 9% (RWF 25M to 100M), 8% (RWF 100M and above), based on your active capital after checkout Taken from each payout, at the rate locked when you invested
Seller on resale 2% of the sale price At settlement
Buyer on resale Nothing
Anyone withdrawing No Rozine fee; your provider's charge only At withdrawal

Rozine takes no share of late charges, no interest spread and nothing from a default. If a raise does not fill, nobody pays a fee.

9. If something goes wrong

9.1. Our mistakes. If Rozine causes you a loss, for example through a ledger error or staff misconduct, Rozine will compensate you in full from its own money. Losses because a business does not pay are the risk you accept and are not compensated.

9.2. Complaints. You can complain in the app, by email to info@rozine.rw, or on WhatsApp Business. You get a reference number, an answer within 4 hours that we have it, and a resolution within 48 hours, or an explanation of why it will take longer and when to expect it. You may take your complaint to the CMA at any time.

9.3. If Rozine stops operating. We stop new raises, tell you and the CMA, and refund every commitment in raises that have not filled. Notes already issued continue to be collected and paid out to the end of their terms. You can withdraw your whole wallet balance free of charge.

9.4. Limits of our liability. Apart from section 9.1, and as far as Rwandan law allows, Rozine is not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for losses caused by a business not paying, a business failing, or events outside our control.

10. General

10.1. Changes to these Terms. We tell you before any change takes effect. When the wording changes, you see the new version and agree to it before you carry on using Rozine. A change never alters the terms of a note that has already been issued.

10.2. Ending your account. You can close your account once you have no open commitments, notes or balances. We keep the records the law requires, as explained in the Privacy Notice.

10.3. Language. These Terms are in English. If they are ever translated, the English version applies.

10.4. Law. These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Rwanda, and the courts of Rwanda decide any dispute.

10.5. Contact. Rozine Technologies Ltd, Kigali, Rwanda · info@rozine.rw

Rozine Privacy Notice

Version privacy-2026-11-23 · Effective 23 November 2026 · Issued by Rozine Technologies Ltd (TIN 156642791), Kigali, Rwanda

This notice explains what personal data Rozine collects, why, where it is kept, who sees it and the rights you have. It applies to everyone who uses Rozine: visitors, investors, businesses, Audit Partners and Rozine staff. When you sign up, you tick a box to confirm you have read it. We record the version and the exact time.

The short version

  • We collect only what we need to run Rozine safely and to meet the law.
  • Your data is stored on servers in Germany, in the European Union. It is not stored in Rwanda.
  • We never sell your data. We share it only with regulators, payment providers and our email provider, as listed below.
  • You can see, correct or ask us to delete your data, subject to the records the law makes us keep.

1. Who we are and the law we follow

1.1. Rozine Technologies Ltd ("Rozine", "we") decides how and why your personal data is used. We follow Law N° 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy in Rwanda.

1.2. Rozine is applying to the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) to register as a data controller and data processor.

1.3. For any privacy question or request, write to info@rozine.rw.

2. What we collect

2.1. Account details. Your name, email address, password (stored only as a one-way hash), language and display settings, and your two-factor sign-in settings.

2.2. Identity checks (KYC). Your full legal name, date of birth, address, National ID or passport details, and the identity documents you upload. For an institution or a business: its official name, Tax Identification Number (TIN), registration documents, directors, owners and the name and address of its representative. We do not collect fingerprints or face scans.

2.3. Screening results. The outcome of checks against sanctions and politically exposed person lists.

2.4. Money and investment records. Your linked Mobile Money (MTN or Airtel) numbers and bank accounts, deposits, withdrawals, wallet balances, commitments, notes, resales, payouts and fees.

2.5. Business records. For businesses: bank and Mobile Money statements, monthly figures, photos of the business, the location of its premises, the prospectus, applications and repayment history.

2.6. Audit records. For Audit Partners: their licence and certificates, office location, declarations of independence, visit reports and the evidence they record.

2.7. Your consents. The version of these documents and of each risk statement you agreed to, and the time you agreed.

2.8. Messages. Complaints, support messages and the notices we send you.

2.9. Technical data. Your IP address, browser and device details, the devices you sign in from, and security logs of sign-ins and important actions.

2.10. Waitlist and calculators. If you join our waitlist or use a calculator on our website, the name, contact details and figures you enter.

3. Why we use it

We use your data only on these lawful grounds:

  • To provide the service you signed up for: opening your account, checking businesses, running raises, collecting repayments, paying out, and handling resales and withdrawals.
  • To meet the law: identity checks, anti-money-laundering checks, investor limits, keeping financial records and reporting to regulators.
  • To keep Rozine safe: preventing fraud, securing accounts and investigating misuse.
  • With your consent: sending you news or marketing. You can withdraw this consent at any time.

Rozine never uses artificial intelligence to make a credit, pricing or investment decision about you. Ratings and offers come from a published formula.

4. Where your data is stored

4.1. Rozine stores your personal, financial and transaction data on a server that Rozine rents from Contabo GmbH, in a data centre in Germany, in the European Union. This includes your account and identity details, the documents you upload, your wallet and transaction records, and security logs. Your data is not stored in Rwanda, and Rozine does not keep copies of it in any other country.

4.2. When Rozine sends you an email, your name, email address and the content of that email are passed to our email provider, Resend, Inc., which processes them in the United States to deliver the message. Resend does not store your other data.

4.3. Data travelling between your device, our servers and our email provider is encrypted. Rozine is applying to the NCSA for the registration that Article 50 of Law N° 058/2021 requires to store personal data outside Rwanda.

4.4. Our test site, staging.rozine.rw, holds only test accounts and test data. Its uploaded test files are stored with Cloudflare in Western Europe. Real customer data is never copied to the test site. Please do not upload real documents there.

5. Who we share it with

We never sell, rent or trade your personal data. We share it only with:

  • Regulators and authorities: the Capital Market Authority (CMA), the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), the NCSA and the Financial Intelligence Centre, when the law requires it.
  • Payment providers: MTN Rwanda, Airtel Rwanda and banks, to move money in and out of wallets. The bank that holds the client account will receive the records it needs.
  • Our email provider: Resend, Inc., as described in section 4.2.
  • Audit Partners: the CPA assigned to a business sees that business's records so they can verify them.
  • Other users, only where the service needs it:
    • Investors see a business's name, rating, prospectus and sealed reports.
    • A business sees how much was raised, but never the names of its investors.
    • Resale buyers and sellers do not see each other's names.

6. How long we keep it

6.1. We keep your data while your account is open.

6.2. After you close your account, we keep financial and identity records for as long as Rwandan financial, tax and anti-money-laundering laws require, then delete them.

6.3. Ledger entries, consents and sealed audit reports can never be edited. They are kept as permanent records for as long as the law requires.

7. How we protect it

7.1. Access to personal data is limited to the staff who need it for their role. Staff need two-factor sign-in, and their important actions are logged with their name.

7.2. If a personal-data breach happens, we will report it to the NCSA within 48 hours and tell the people affected.

8. Cookies

Rozine uses only the cookies it needs to work: one to keep you signed in and secure your session, and others to remember your language and light or dark display. We use no advertising or tracking cookies.

9. Your rights

Under Law N° 058/2021 you have the right to:

  • See your data: ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you.
  • Correct it: have wrong or incomplete data corrected.
  • Delete it: ask us to delete your data, except where the law requires us to keep it.
  • Object or withdraw consent: stop marketing messages at any time, and object to uses based on our legitimate interests.
  • Complain: contact us first at info@rozine.rw. You may also complain to the NCSA.

We answer every request within 30 days.

10. Changes to this notice

If we change this notice, for example if we move your data or start using a new provider that receives it, we will publish the new version first and ask you to read it before you carry on using Rozine.

legal_documents.title: Disclaimers
legal_documents.html:
Rozine Disclaimers

Version disclaimers-2026-11-23-r2 · Effective 23 November 2026 · Issued by Rozine Technologies Ltd (TIN 156642791), Kigali, Rwanda

This page brings together every warning that appears on Rozine, word for word where it is shown in the apps, and explains what each one means for you. When you sign up, you tick a box to confirm you have read and understood them. We record the version and the exact time. These disclaimers form part of our Terms and Conditions.

1. The CMA sandbox notice

Shown: before the sign-up form, on the investor risk screen and in our marketing.

Rozine is testing this service in the Capital Market Authority's Fintech Regulatory Sandbox, under limits set by the CMA. Admission to the sandbox is not a licence or an endorsement.

What it means: the CMA's sandbox lets new financial services be tried under close watch and strict limits. The CMA has admitted Rozine to its sandbox. Being in the sandbox does not mean the CMA has licensed Rozine, approved any business on it, or checked any investment.

2. The risk warning

Shown: on our website, on every listing and at checkout.

Investing carries risk, including loss of capital. Returns are not guaranteed.

What it means: you lend your money to a real business. If the business cannot pay, you can get back less than you put in, or nothing at all.

3. The five risk statements

Shown: once, after your identity is verified and before your wallet opens. You tick one box: "I understand all of the above". If the wording changes, you see it again.

  • I can lose all the money I invest.
  • There is no guarantee or collateral.
  • Returns are paid only if the business pays.
  • I may not find a buyer if I want to sell early.
  • Rozine operates in the CMA sandbox under limits.

What they mean:

  • You can lose everything. A note is an unsecured loan. If the business fails, recovery may return little or nothing.
  • Nothing backs your money. There is no collateral, guarantee, insurance or reserve fund behind any note, and Rozine does not cover losses.
  • You are paid only when the business pays. Rozine passes on what it collects. It does not advance payments from its own money.
  • Selling early is not certain. Resale needs another investor willing to buy at your price.
  • Limits apply. The sandbox caps how big Rozine can grow, and the CMA can change or end it.

4. Rozine is a platform, not a lender

Shown: in the Terms and in help answers.

Rozine connects businesses and investors and runs the note. Rozine never lends its own money, guarantees capital or returns, buys or sells notes, makes a market or sets resale prices. Rozine is not a bank, a microfinance institution, a deposit-taker or an insurer. Your wallet and your notes are not insured by the Government of Rwanda, the National Bank of Rwanda or the CMA.

5. No investment advice

Shown: on ratings, deals and the prospectus.

Rozine does not advise you or recommend any investment. Rating labels, such as Strong, Stable or Distressed, and returns come from a published formula applied to verified facts. They describe a business's risk; they do not tell you to invest. Decide for yourself, and get independent advice if you need it. Spreading your money across several notes lowers, but does not remove, the risk.

6. Returns and schedules are not promises

Shown: next to returns and schedules, for example "Returns are projected, not guaranteed" at checkout and "Scheduled, not guaranteed" in your portfolio.

A note's return and repayment schedule are what the business has agreed to pay. They are not a promise that it will. Past repayments by a business, or across Rozine, do not tell you what will happen in future.

7. Late charges

Shown: in your portfolio when a note is late.

Late charges and penalty fees are accrued daily upon default and are payable to note holders only as and when collected from the borrower. Rozine does not guarantee or advance late fee recoveries.

What it means: late charges are added to what the business owes. You receive your share only if and when the business actually pays them.

8. Fee figures

Shown: at checkout.

The exact fee is worked out on each repayment once your notes are reserved, so it can differ by a few francs.

What it means: the earnings fee is a percentage of each return payment, rounded to whole francs. The total you see at checkout is an estimate that can differ by a few francs from the sum of the actual fees.

9. Business information and CPA checks

Shown: on listings, prospectuses and audit reports.

Business figures come from the statements the business uploads and from an independent Certified Public Accountant's in-person checks. A CPA check makes errors and fraud much less likely, but it is not a guarantee that every figure is correct or that the business will succeed. Rozine is not liable for false information a business gives, though we act on it when we find it.

10. Selling early

Shown: in the resale market.

A sale needs a buyer, so it is never guaranteed. You may have to lower your price, or keep the note to the end of its term. Trading pauses around each due date, and the market can be halted.

11. Where your money is held

All customer money is to be held in a segregated client account at a licensed Rwandan commercial bank. We are in talks with GT Bank to provide that account; no agreement has been signed yet. Rozine will not take real customer money until the account is open.

12. Where your data is held

Your data is stored on servers in Germany, in the European Union, not in Rwanda. Rozine is applying to the National Cyber Security Authority for the registration needed to store personal data outside Rwanda. See our Privacy Notice.

13. Calculators, examples and the waitlist

Shown: on our website, for example "Non-binding demand simulation" and the return calculators.

Calculators, examples and sample figures on our website are illustrations. They are not offers, quotes or promises. Your real figures are shown in the app before you confirm anything. Joining the waitlist does not commit you to anything and does not guarantee you a place in any raise.

14. Test site and simulated money

Shown: on staging.rozine.rw.

staging.rozine.rw is a test site. Businesses, deals, wallets, payments, disbursements, repayments, resales and payouts there may be simulated with test data. No real money moves, and nothing on the test site is an offer to invest.

15. Taxes

You are responsible for any tax due on your returns or your business's income. Rozine does not give tax advice.

16. Language and translations

Rozine's screens are available in English, French and Kinyarwanda. Our legal documents are in English. If a translation ever differs, the English version applies.

17. Links to other websites

Links to other websites are for your information only. Rozine is not responsible for their content.
